- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is trending up, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) and sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, model tends to overestimate — cap forecast rise at 3–5% above recent high.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a dip (e.g., 3–5% jump from low), reduce by 10–15% to avoid overshoot — especially if sentiment is weak or negative.  
- When sentiment is positive (especially > 0.3) and forecast is flat or slightly down, increase forecast by 2–5% to capture sentiment-driven rally.  
- If true outcome consistently lags forecast by 1–2 days (especially in early week), adjust forecast to be 1–2% lower than model for next period to account for lag.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 10-day moving average, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence — especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >15% above recent 18-day high, apply downward correction of 5–8% to avoid overestimating short-term volatility.
